correctness.rationale: Orthogonal Gaussian regression gives the reciprocal FOM coefficient exactly as a normal/chi ratio with continuous positive density at zero; the integral of |h|^{-p} near zero diverges exactly for p>=1. Regressing Sb on SAb gives direct normal/chi for the GMRES coefficient with Student tail threshold p<s. Almost-sure denominator existence, sharp t^-1 constant, negative sign probability, and finite GMRES residual formula follow explicitly. Finite checker supports the derived constants; the proof establishes infinite moments.

broader_coverage.reasoning: High-probability or embedding-conditioned bounds do not imply finite unconditional moments; a fixed bad-sketch tail can have arbitrarily small probability and still diverge. The general MR/OR structural relation does not give these Gaussian moment thresholds.

evidence: Güttel–Schweitzer observe nonpositive sketched Ritz values and irregular approximation norms.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The existence of instability does not logically imply a universal infinite first moment at every finite s, an exact t^{-1} coefficient, or the finite second-moment criterion for the matched sketched GMRES. These assertions require the normal/chi ratio distributions and endpoint integration proved here; conversely the new theorem does not replace the source general convergence analysis.

evidence: Güttel–Schweitzer sFOM equation (5) and section 2.3; positive-real input may have negative sketched Ritz values.
Timsit–Grigori–Balabanov section 3 and numerical section discuss randomized Petrov–Galerkin projection and occasional spikes.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same one-dimensional Petrov–Galerkin coefficient is present algebraically in the source method, but the sources do not identify its reciprocal Student distribution, all finite-height moment thresholds, or exact probability and tail constant. Gaussian-regression Student laws themselves are elementary and not claimed original.

evidence: The relevant Krylov references contain sketched solver definitions, norm bounds, projected spectral behavior and numerical tests, but no cited finite-sketch exact distribution table for this pair of coefficient estimators.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The claim is a continuous all-moment statement, not a numerical table lookup or previously tabulated special value. Explicit elementary s=3 constants serve as witnesses, not the main novelty.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons locate preexisting sketched projection formulas, negative Ritz outliers, high-probability quasi-optimality, and MR/OR pairing, but not the exact Gaussian one-step reciprocal Student law, sharp all-moment failure for FOM and finite-variance GMRES contrast. The elementary Student-regression mechanism is credited as classical; precedence may survive in less-visible specialist literature.
residual_risks: Elementary Gaussian-ratio and randomized Galerkin specialist literature might contain equivalent all-moment results under different terminology.
The comparator source arxiv:1803.02602 was not independently material-read in its full text during this review.
Semantic/indexed searches do not prove global novelty.

value.rationale: An exact universal risk classification distinguishes two widely used one-step sketched Krylov methods on any nontrivial SPD input; rare bad sketches cause unbounded unconditional first moment despite arbitrarily large finite oversampling, while the matched residual-minimizing method has finite variance for s>2. It gives an exact negative-Ritz failure probability and a tail constant, motivating true residual checks/regularization rather than relying on typical convergence plots.
